questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A client with new confusion repeatedly pulls at oxygen tubing. Which action should the RN take first while maintaining immediate safety?
choices: Apply wrist restraints before assessing the client
Assess oxygenation, pain, toileting needs, delirium cues, and what the client is trying to accomplish
Request a standing restraint order for the remainder of the admission
Administer a sedating medication solely to prevent movement
questions.explanation: Pulling at equipment is a cue that requires assessment for reversible causes while immediate safety is maintained. Hypoxia, pain, delirium, fear, or toileting needs may be addressed without restraint.

questions.question: A family member asks the RN to restrain an alert client because the family is afraid the client might fall. Which response is best?
choices: A family request is enough authorization for restraint
Restraint is required for every client identified as a fall risk
We will assess the client’s individual risks and use the least restrictive effective safety plan; restraint cannot be used only for convenience or routine fall prevention
The family may apply a restraint without an order if they remain in the room
questions.explanation: Restraint requires clinical necessity and the applicable authorization process; fear or family preference alone is insufficient. The RN uses an individualized fall-prevention plan and least restrictive measures.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which medication use may meet the definition of a restraint?
choices: An antibiotic given at the prescribed dose for a bacterial infection
An analgesic titrated according to an order for reported postoperative pain
A routine home medication continued for its documented indication
A sedating medication used mainly to control behavior or restrict movement when it is not standard treatment or dosage for the client’s condition
questions.explanation: A medication can function as a restraint when its primary purpose is behavior control or movement restriction and it is not standard treatment or dosage for the client’s condition. The drug name alone does not determine this.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A client suddenly swings a metal object at another client and cannot be redirected. What is the RN’s priority action?
choices: Summon trained assistance, move others from danger, use de-escalation, and follow the emergency process for the least restrictive effective intervention
Approach alone and attempt to take the object by force
Wait until a routine team meeting before intervening
Lock the unit doors and leave both clients together
questions.explanation: An immediate serious threat requires rapid protection of everyone present, trained assistance, hazard reduction, and de-escalation. Any restrictive intervention must be the least restrictive effective option under the emergency process.

questions.question: Which assessment finding in a restrained client requires the most immediate response?
choices: The client asks what time breakfast will arrive
The client reports mild boredom
The restrained hand is cool and pale with delayed capillary refill
The client requests the television remote
questions.explanation: Coolness, pallor, and delayed capillary refill suggest impaired circulation and possible tissue injury. The RN immediately protects the client, releases or adjusts the intervention as appropriate, and follows the urgent response process.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: A restrained client is now calm, follows directions, and no longer presents the behavior that created immediate danger. What should the RN do?
choices: Continue restraint until the full order time expires
Discontinue the restraint at the earliest safe time and continue the individualized safety plan
Wait for the family to approve release
Renew the order so the restraint is available if behavior returns
questions.explanation: Restraint must end as soon as the unsafe situation has resolved, regardless of remaining time on the order. The RN continues observation and an individualized plan rather than restraining for a possible future behavior.

questions.question: Which restraint order should the RN question?
choices: An order entered after assessment for a specific current safety need
An order with reassessment requirements defined by current policy
A time-limited order from an authorized practitioner
A standing PRN order to apply restraints whenever the client becomes restless
questions.explanation: Hospital restraint rules do not permit standing or PRN restraint orders. Each use requires assessment of a current clinical need, the applicable authorization, ongoing reassessment, and discontinuation at the earliest safe time.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: Which statement about four raised side rails is most accurate?
choices: Side rails can never be considered a restraint
Any single raised rail is always a restraint
Whether the rails function as a restraint depends on their purpose, use, and whether they restrict the client from voluntarily leaving the bed
Side rails are restraints only when the family objects
questions.explanation: Equipment is evaluated by how it affects the individual client, not by its label alone. Rails that prevent voluntary exit may function as a restraint; therapeutic use and definitions depend on current rules and policy.

questions.question: Which documentation entry best supports safe restraint care?
choices: Client difficult; restraint used for safety
Restraint continued because the previous shift started it
Client restless; no further details needed

Client repeatedly struck staff with the call-light cord; pain and toileting assessed, de-escalation and reduced stimulation ineffective; required order obtained, monitoring begun, and response documented
questions.explanation: Useful documentation states the observable behavior and risk, assessment findings, alternatives and responses, clinical reason, authorization, monitoring, and outcome. Vague labels do not establish necessity or continuity.

questions.nclexClientNeeds: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control
questions.question: For which situation may seclusion be considered under applicable hospital rules after less restrictive measures are ineffective or unsafe?
choices: A client with violent behavior presents an immediate physical danger to others
A client repeatedly uses the call light for assistance
A client with dementia wanders toward the dayroom
A client refuses a scheduled bath
questions.explanation: Seclusion is limited to management of violent or self-destructive behavior that creates an immediate physical safety threat. It is not an intervention for inconvenience, wandering, treatment refusal, or frequent requests.
